chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Juʿfī, who said:

I used to go repeatedly to Ibn Abī Laylā regarding inheritances belonging to us so that he might divide them, and there was a ḥabīs in it, so he kept putting me off. When that became prolonged, I complained about him to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
So he said: “Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered the return of the ḥabīs and the execution of the inheritances?”
He said: So I went to him, and he acted as he had been acting. Then I said to him: “I complained about you to Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, and he said to me such-and-such and such-and-such.”
He said: Ibn Abī Laylā then made me swear that he had indeed said that, so I swore to him, and he judged for me accordingly.

key_terms.إِنْفَاذِ: putting into effect or carrying out
key_terms.حَبِيسٌ: property withheld or restricted from transfer within the estate
key_terms.فَحَلَّفَنِي: he made me swear an oath
key_terms.مَوَارِيثَ: inheritances or shares of estate to be divided among heirs
key_terms.يُدَافِعُنِي: he kept delaying me or putting me off

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about returning a ḥabīs and carrying out inheritance distribution?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a dispute over inheritance in which a restricted holding prevented proper division of an estate. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام cites the command of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that such a ḥabīs be returned and inheritances be duly executed, and this statement ultimately leads to a ruling in the claimant’s favor.
